narrative: Material PL1__M5F3FB32 shows smooth, normally-distributed demand (CV=0.149) with no detectable trend across 93 working days. Lead times are highly variable (CV=1.24) despite a short mean of 0.76 days, making lead-time variability the dominant driver of the safety stock requirement. An (r,Q) continuous-review policy is recommended, with the EOQ capped at 160,260 units due to the storage constraint of 167,788 units. Consolidating from ~42 to ~8 orders per year yields 77.5% total cost savings while maintaining the 95% service level.
warnings: EOQ (311,664) exceeds storage capacity; order quantity capped to 160,260 units (max_storage - safety_stock = 160,260).
Lead time CV=1.24 classified as unstable; monitor supplier performance closely.

research_insights.selection_rationale: Demand is smooth and fully continuous (CV=0.149, 100% non-zero days), making a continuous-review model optimal. The short but volatile lead time (mean 0.76d, CV 1.24) is captured analytically in sigma_LTD, avoiding the need for periodic review buffers. Fixed Q at EOQ (storage-capped) minimises total cost.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage cap binds: EOQ of 311,664 is reduced to 160,260. This increases order frequency from the unconstrained optimum (~3.9 orders/yr) to 7.5 orders/yr, adding ~$187/yr in ordering cost relative to unconstrained EOQ. Service level is unaffected as safety stock is unchanged.
